intro: Stop 0. You are looking at the What?? panel. Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honour all of them. Today's roll was seed 4273567032. Please proceed through the rolls in order, and do not shake the gift.

rolls.value: 🎁 a wrapped gift who hates surprises
rolls.became: The museum's Unopened Gift, 1911. It hates surprises for the best possible reason: it is one, and it has never been allowed to know what's inside itself. The museum decided the mystery was the exhibit.

Some minerals really do store light and give it back slowly (that's phosphorescence: glow-in-the-dark). The gift lives in the Mineral Hall, so it charges the crystals with moonlight, and their glow is what it holds itself up to.

The gift still sits on the delivery trolley it arrived on in 1911. After closing it steers the trolley round the hall, with a borrowed magnifying lens that focuses the skylight's moonlight into a hot little spot.

What's in the box? Every Peek empties the jars through the gift in one flash and sees one layer deeper: the ribbon, the paper, the tape, the box, the tissue, a second box (we don't discuss the second box), the bubble wrap, the velvet.

Paper scatters light, and every layer underneath needs a brighter flash. Glow fades as crystals give it off, the jars only hold so much, and velvet only lets a full spectrum through. The audio guide would like it noted that none of this is the gift's fault.
The gift tag, face-down for a century, says “For C.” The gift spends a lot of the game wondering who C. is.
Case 24 of the collection, the sky-blue crystal labelled “missing since 1911”. It was posted to the museum in 1911. It never went missing. It was in the gift. C. was never a who: it was a what.
The cabinet under the hall: 24 cases in four rooms (Quartz, Corundum, Beryl, Glow). Every crystal you find takes a stand in the hall, and a complete room glows twice as bright.

rolls.value: a recipe book: combine things to discover new ones
rolls.became: Real mineralogy on the bench. Quartz with iron (pyrite) is amethyst, corundum with chromium is ruby, beryl with manganese is morganite, quartz left in the moonbeam goes smoky, and amethyst warmed on the 1911 radiator turns into citrine. The empty cases give hints.

rolls.value: storage caps you must build past
rolls.became: Each layer needs a bigger flash than the jars can hold, so you build up: jam jars, a bell jar from the Clocks gallery, a carboy, the old cistern, a gas holder, the planetarium dome, and finally the whole East Wing (closed for refurbishment since 1974).
Eight layers, 23 crystals to find and a lot of jars. Revolving lamps off an old carousel keep the crystals topped up while you're away, so the jars are fuller when you come back.
The first Peek takes 300 glow. The last takes 10 billion.
Ten billion glow in the jars and every crystal in the hall, for one last flash through the velvet pouch.

The last flash shows the gift Celestine, and then Celestine charges. It throws the light back up through the skylight, and at 3am the whole town sees the inside of the gift drawn on the clouds. The gift that hated surprises becomes the biggest surprise the town has ever had. The Gentle Shake's “tink” was Celestine all along.

A 320×180 hall drawn pixel by pixel: the gift and its trolley hand-made, crystals as little three-colour pixel grids, icons pixelated down from open-licensed shapes, and an x-ray inset that clears one layer per Peek.
Sixteen pastels by Space Sandwich: plum floors, lilac and mint glows, a butter-yellow ribbon, a coral gift. A museum at night, in milkshake.

Mineral Hall After Hours: a late-night trio with a walking upright bass, brushes and soft vibraphone, all on the five notes of A hirajoshi (A B C E F), the same five notes every chime in the game uses. The keys join as the layers come off.
The log is the audio guide, numbering its stops and keeping very calm about a parcel driving itself round the Mineral Hall. It slowly comes round to the gift's side.
The gift arrived on 5 November 1911, the day the first aeroplane to fly across America landed in Pasadena. The gift came by train. It would like that noted. (It's the 1911 Postcard upgrade.)

outro: That concludes the tour. Please exit through the gift.
